question: Should trusted spawned and fallback internal sessions inherit a stored effective sender-policy projection, or should only verified subagent envelopes bypass sender-policy re-resolution?
rationale: Both approaches can restore delegated tools, but the permanent trust boundary determines which internal session kinds may retain requester authority without external sender identity; choosing too broad a bypass could overgrant tools.

options.title: Carry Effective Policy
options.body: Persist and consume a trusted normalized effective sender policy for verified internal descendants, then intersect it with ordinary subagent restrictions and test both spawn and fallback paths.

options.title: Envelope-Only Bypass
options.body: Skip sender-policy resolution only for verified subagent envelopes, accepting that other internal continuation paths need separate handling or remain restricted.

options.title: Keep Fail-Closed Behavior
options.body: Continue applying wildcard policy when sender identity is absent, preserving the current restriction at the cost of breaking delegated workflows using exact overrides.

recommendation.title: Carry Effective Policy
recommendation.body: Persist and consume a trusted normalized effective sender policy for verified internal descendants, then intersect it with ordinary subagent restrictions and test both spawn and fallback paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent session, tool-policy, and authorization-sensitive work makes this the best available routing candidate, though exact module ownership is not definitive.
